sources.entry: ClearanceKit - Policy-based file access control tool for protected paths. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/craigjbass/clearancekit) ![Native App][Native Icon]

summary.name: ClearanceKit
summary.one_liner: A macOS kernel-level file access control tool that restricts which file paths each process may open or modify, based on the process's code-signing identity.
use_cases: Stop a compromised package install script from reading SSH, cloud, or git credentials
Restrict which paths a specific app or process can read or write
Review denied file access events on a Mac
Deploy file access policies across a managed fleet via MDM
Confine a process to an explicit set of allowed path prefixes
summary.what_it_does: ClearanceKit is a macOS tool that enforces file access policies at the kernel level using Endpoint Security AUTH events. When a process calls open, rename, unlink, or another file-system syscall, the request is forwarded to its opfilter component, which checks the caller's code-signing identity against policies and returns ALLOW or DENY. Policies match on Team ID and Signing ID rather than path or hash, so they persist across software updates from the same signer. It also supports jail rules that confine a process to listed path prefixes (inherited by children) and rules requiring a trusted parent process. A native SwiftUI interface shows denied events, a live throughput graph, and lets users build policy without config files. Policies can also be delivered through standard Apple Configuration Profile payloads for MDM.
notable: Policies bound to Team ID and Signing ID, so they survive software updates
Jail rules confine processes to explicit path prefixes, inherited by child processes
Zero network calls and no third-party dependencies; built on Apple frameworks
MDM fleet management via standard Apple Configuration Profile payloads
caveats: No auto-update; new versions must be checked and installed manually from the releases page
Requires granting Full Disk Access and activating a system extension during install
